meta.title: Hiking trails and groups — Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRG) and Federal Iraq
meta.scope: Real, publicly documented walks, peaks, and arrangers. Distances/times are typical published figures, not surveyed GPS unless noted.
honesty_notes: Iraq has almost no waymarked day-hike network outside the Zagros Mountain Trail (ZMT). Most 'trails' are shepherds' paths, 4x4 tracks, or picnic walks.
Landmines and UXO from the Iran–Iraq War, Anfal, and later conflicts are a real constraint. Stay on used tracks; hire a local guide on high mountains.
Cheekha Dar / Qandil approaches are not a normal tourist product. Included only because they are geographically famous, with safety flags.
Jabal Sinjar is not a commonly advertised tourist hike. Federal Iraq (Khanaqin, Hamrin, etc.) has picnic hills, not a hiking scene.
Instagram/Facebook handles are included only when they appear on official operator sites, ZMT service-provider pages, or clearly public profiles. None were invented.
TakeYourBackpack-style auto-guides sometimes invent start towns (e.g. Kifri for Halgurd). Those figures were discarded.

Cheekha Dar (approx. 3,611 m) is often listed as Iraq's highest peak; many Kurdish climbers treat Halgurd (3,607 m) as the highest fully Iraqi summit because Cheekha Dar sits on the Iran border and is effectively off-limits.
Season for almost all KRG mountain hiking: April–June and September–November. July–August is brutally hot except at high altitude or canyon water. December–March is snow/ice on 2,500 m+ peaks.
sources_used: https://www.zagrosmountaintrail.org/ and its stage + service-provider pages
Wanderlust, FAO Mountain Partnership, Abraham Path / Kurdistan Trails for Development
Public operator sites: visitiraqikurdistan.com, kurdistanoutdoor.com, kurdistanexpeditions.com, mesopotamiatourism.com

trails.nearest_town: Starts Shush (Akre district, Duhok); ends Choman / Halgurd base (Erbil governorate)
trails.approx_hours: 13 walking days (typically 4–12 hours/day); 10–15 days with rest
trails.season: April–June, September–November. High stages hold snow into May.
trails.typical_start_point: Village of Shush (Şûş), west of Akre; many groups reverse-hike Stage 1 from Akre citadel.
trails.notable: Iraq's first long-distance hiking route. 13 stages linking 30–36 villages on old pilgrimage, trading and shepherd paths. Community homestays and local guides. Created by local/international hikers (Leon McCarron, Emily Garthwaite and Kurdish partners); managed by Kurdistan Trails for Development; official launch Oct 2023 / public walking from 2024. Not fully waymarked. Passes Akre, Barzan valley, Rawanduz gorge, Bradost, Hindren/Karokh saddle, ends at Halgurd base.
trails.uncertainty: Stage numbering of the last two days varies slightly across operator writeups (Rezan–Choman vs Choman–Halgurd base). Total 215 km is the official figure.
trails.guide_required: Strongly recommended; ZMT official site says hire a local guide.
trails.landmine_uxo: Yes on some ridgelines (notably Bradost 4x4 track above Khalan–Soran). Stay on used track.

trails.season: March–November; spring wildflowers; Newroz (around 20–21 March) is the town's big festival.
trails.typical_start_point: Shush village (synagogue remains, old church, community leader Nader's homestay) or reverse from Akre citadel / town centre.
trails.notable: Official ZMT opener. Pine forest drop into Akre, one of Kurdistan's most photogenic hill towns and the 'capital of Newroz'. Passes Gundki monastery ruins and a cave with poorly preserved ancient reliefs. Wide 4x4/animal tracks; one clay/exposed-drop section in rain.
trails.uncertainty: Official ZMT: 16.5 km, +760 m, difficulty Medium.
trails.guide_required: Recommended but this stage is among the more walked and 'ready'.
trails.landmine_uxo: Not flagged as a primary mine stage.

trails.season: March–November
trails.typical_start_point: Akre town; ends Hashtga village (hilltop homestay).
trails.notable: Short mountain-fortress / shepherd-country stage used as a one-day taster by Erbil groups. Often combined with Stage 1 as a weekend.
trails.uncertainty: 8.2 km / +530 m comes from public group-hike posts, not the official stage page (not retrieved). Official km may differ.
trails.guide_required: Recommended. Local guide Sadiq Khuder Izzo is the named Stage 1–2 specialist.
trails.landmine_uxo: Not specifically flagged.

trails.nearest_town: Safti / Alka (between Akre and Barzan country)
trails.season: April–June, September–November (waterfalls strongest in spring)
trails.typical_start_point: Safti village (Anwer Salih Muhammad homestay/guide).
trails.notable: Repeatedly called one of the best ZMT days: lush valleys, stacked waterfalls, possible side-walk to the Isumera/Isumara ruin. Official: +950 m, Hard.
trails.uncertainty: Ruin dating ('Sumerian') is local/guide lore, not independently verified here.
trails.guide_required: Yes — unwaymarked, seasonal river/waterfall terrain.
trails.landmine_uxo: Not the main mine stage; still hire local knowledge.

trails.name_en: Gali Ali Beg / Hamilton Road gorge
trails.name_ku: گەلی عەلی بەگ / ڕێگای هامیلتۆن (Gelî Elî Beg)
trails.approx_km: 1–4 for waterfall viewpoints and old-road half-tunnel; Hamilton Road itself is a ~185 km historic highway, not a trail
trails.approx_hours: 1–3 for the waterfall / old-road walk; full road is a drive
trails.season: Year-round sightseeing. Summer is packed with families from Baghdad/Basra escaping heat. Spring for green canyon walls.
trails.typical_start_point: Hamilton Road pull-offs at Gali Ali Beg waterfall; or the Archibald Hamilton bust at Kawlukan below Rawanduz.
trails.notable: Kurdistan's most famous canyon/waterfall and the scenic spine of the historic Hamilton Road (built 1928–32 by A.M. Hamilton). Highest waterfall in the region; half-tunnel of the original road cut into the cliff. More of a spectacular roadside/short-walk destination than a wilderness trail. Hiking trails do peel off into forested slopes and toward Bekhal.
trails.uncertainty: There is no single official 'Gali Ali Beg trail' with a fixed km. Treat as a canyon corridor with multiple short walks.
trails.guide_required: Not for the waterfall viewpoint. Yes for leaving the road into side canyons.
trails.landmine_uxo: Main tourist strip is cleared/used. Do not wander off-track into side slopes.

trails.name_en: Bekhal waterfall and Rawanduz canyon walk
trails.nearest_town: Rawanduz; Bekhal is ~8 km south of town
trails.approx_km: Waterfall itself is a short walk from parking. Canyon trek from Hamilton bust toward Bekhal: ~3.5 km out-and-back on one Wikiloc track (2.16 mi); continuing all the way is described as unstable.
trails.approx_hours: 0.5–1 at the falls; 2–4 for a canyon-rim or in-canyon walk
trails.season: April–November; summer swimming/picnic crowds; spring for flow
trails.typical_start_point: Bekhal waterfall parking (upper and lower approaches exist); or Hamilton statue at Kawlukan for the in-canyon path.
trails.notable: Twin to Gali Ali Beg on the same Hamilton Road corridor. Multi-tier falls, restaurants, tea places. The Rawanduz canyon rim is also ZMT Stage 8. Kharand Rawanduz viewpoint is an easy 1-hour walk. A proposed future cable car would link Ali Beg gorge toward Korek.
trails.uncertainty: Online '5 km one-way hike to Bekhal' figures look inflated for the falls themselves. The falls are a developed tourist site.
trails.guide_required: No for the falls. Yes for committing to the inner-canyon continuation.
trails.landmine_uxo: Tourist zone is used daily. Off-path canyon walls are not.

trails.name_en: ZMT Stage 8 — Soran to Rawanduz (canyon rim)
trails.season: March–November
trails.typical_start_point: Soran (Soran Palace / Palas Hotel is the named trailhead hotel).
trails.notable: Official ZMT: +572 m, Easy. Climbs to a picnic plateau with Korek views, follows the Rawanduz canyon rim, descends to Kawlukan (Hamilton bust) and into Rawanduz. Best 'short scenic day' on the eastern ZMT.
trails.uncertainty: None on official stats.
trails.guide_required: Useful but this is one of the easier, more 'ready' stages.
trails.landmine_uxo: Not the primary mine stage.

trails.nearest_town: Rawanduz / Soran; ~90 km northeast of Erbil
trails.approx_km: AllTrails 'Mount Korek Trail' ~16.4 km (10.2 mi) with ~1,030 m gain; cable car is ~4 km ride to the resort
trails.approx_hours: 6.5–7.5 hiking; or a short resort stroll after the teleferic
trails.season: May–October for hiking. Winter snow play/ski at the resort. Year-round cable car when operating.
trails.typical_start_point: Korek Mountain Resort / cable-car base near Rawanduz; hikers also start from lower access roads toward Hasan Beg / Rawanduz valley views.
trails.notable: Most developed mountain in KRG: 4 km cable car, resort (Radisson Blu / Korek Mountain Resort), restaurants, winter snow. Summit/ridge ~2,030–2,076 m (resort plateau often quoted ~1,700 m). On ZMT Stage 9 the high pass is where Karokh and Hendrin meet — that is a different, wilder approach than the resort. Local oral tradition treats Karokh/Hindren as culturally important peaks.
trails.uncertainty: Elevation figures conflict (1,700 m resort, ~2,030–2,076 m mountain). Radisson marketing that says 3,612 m is wrong (that is Halgurd/Cheekha Dar height). Hiking km depends entirely on whether you use the cable car.
trails.guide_required: No for resort walks. Yes for a full ridge traverse or linking toward Hindren.
trails.landmine_uxo: Resort area is developed. Connecting ridges toward older military roads need a guide.

trails.approx_km: Summit day commonly quoted ~12–20 km round trip from high trailhead/base; ZMT Stage 13 to base is 16.3 km one way from Choman
trails.approx_hours: Summit: 8–10 hours round trip from the high start; Choman to base is a separate 9–10 hour uphill day (+1,455 m). Many parties camp at base.
trails.season: Late June–October for non-technical walk-up. Snow/ice 9–10 months; spring can still need axe/experience. Best: July–September for locals; September–October for cooler air.
trails.typical_start_point: Choman → dirt roads toward Halgurd to the last driveable point / old stone buildings at 'Halgurd Base' (~2,250 m). Do not start from Kifri (a common auto-guide error).
trails.notable: 3,607 m. Treated by most Kurdish climbers as Iraq's highest fully Iraqi peak. Inside the proposed/partial Halgurd–Sakran National Park (~1,000 km² highland). Non-technical but long, rocky, mined off-trail. Permit historically issued via Kurdistan Mountaineering and Climbing Federation (reported free for foreigners). Omar Chomani / VIKurdistan is the established local operator for base camp and summit.
trails.uncertainty: Round-trip km varies with how far vehicles get. Cheekha Dar (3,611 m) is slightly higher but on the Iran border and not a normal climb.
trails.guide_required: Yes. Official ZMT: hire a trusted guide; mines further up the mountain.
trails.landmine_uxo: YES. UXO signs around 2,250 m. Stay on the wide 4x4 track. Summit only with a guide who knows the line.

trails.name_en: ZMT Stage 13 — Choman to Halgurd Base
trails.season: June–October; snow possible much of the year
trails.typical_start_point: Choman town — follow the paved road north ~5 km, then the mountain track to the old stone buildings / nomad camp at Halgurd Base.
trails.notable: Official eastern terminus of the ZMT. +1,455 m. No resupply. Views of Halgurd and toward Sakran. Camping and mountain-house options via Omar Chomani.
trails.uncertainty: None on official stats.
trails.guide_required: Yes
trails.landmine_uxo: YES — UXO signage on the upper 4x4 track.

trails.approx_km: No single official trail. Summit attempts are a long alpine day from a high village start; valley walks around Sakran village are shorter.
trails.approx_hours: Village/valley walks 2–5 hours. Summit: pre-dawn start, often 8+ hours; parties regularly turn around on steep snow.
trails.season: July–September for high peaks (ice axe/rope reported for the technical summit and crater-lake area). Village visits year-round; famous summer escape.
trails.typical_start_point: Sakran village or other Choman-district trailheads inside Halgurd–Sakran National Park.
trails.notable: The other great wall of the Halgurd–Sakran park, SE of Choman. Peaks in the 3,000 m+ class (one public post cites ~3,200 m). Kurdistan Chronicle describes Sakran as a technical climb with ice axe/ropes and a crater lake. Przha snow cave is a known summer feature. Views pair Halgurd (NE) and Sakran (SE) from the Balakayati hills.
trails.uncertainty: No reliable public GPX with agreed km/hours for 'the' Sakran hike. Treat as a mountain range, not one trail.
trails.guide_required: Yes for anything above village walks. Border-adjacent.
trails.landmine_uxo: Assume yes off used tracks. Iran–Iraq War legacy plus border militarization.

trails.name_en: Cheekha Dar (Çîxî Derê) — Hasarost / border high peak
trails.season: Not a seasonal tourism product. Academic/hiker reports mention rare winter/early-spring windows when military presence is thinner — this is not a recommendation.
trails.typical_start_point: Not published as a legal tourist start. Summit has been reported occupied by Iranian forces (pasdaran outpost) with roads pushed into Iraqi territory.
trails.notable: Often listed as Iraq's highest mountain (~3,611 m), pyramid-shaped, on the Iran–Iraq line. User-facing name 'Hasarost' in some lists overlaps the Hasari Sakran highland rather than this single peak. Included only because it is the famous high point next to Halgurd.
trails.uncertainty: Do not treat this as an open hike. Sources (YouTube climbers, 2026 academic paper) say Iranian guards have fired on people approaching; summit occupation makes a legal ascent effectively impossible most of the time.
trails.guide_required: Not a tourist offering.
trails.landmine_uxo: YES, plus active military / border risk.

trails.name_en: Bradost Mountain (ZMT Stage 7 — Khalan to Soran)
trails.approx_hours: 11–12 (longest ZMT stage; often split at Sheikh Sherif)
trails.season: April–June, September–October. Little shade in the middle. Summer is punishing.
trails.typical_start_point: Khalan village (or Qamyran off-trail homestay of Jawad Ibrahim Meer). Ancient stone-reinforced donkey path up Bradost.
trails.notable: The big Bradost day: canyon-side trading path, Saddam-era 1970s military road and ruined village of Sheikh Sherif, forest, then a mined ridgeline 4x4 track with views west over Barzan and east to Hendrin, Hasan Beg and Halgurd. Official: +1,233 m, Hard. Visit Erbil has also promoted Bradost as a >5,000 ft range in the Soran administration.
trails.uncertainty: None on official ZMT stats. Standalone 'Bradost day hikes' exist but are not standardised.
trails.guide_required: Yes — length, exposure, UXO.
trails.landmine_uxo: YES. Signs on the ridgeline 4x4 track. Stay on the used road.

trails.approx_km: ZMT Stage 9 Rawanduz–Saran is 24.1 km (+1,195 m). The Karokh–Hindren meeting is on the high pass used on the Soran/Akoyan–Saran–Dargala sequence (Untamed Borders: 7–8 hours, high point ~2,100 m).
trails.approx_hours: 7–8 for the pass day; Stage 9 can be split at Garawan after 16.5 km
trails.season: May–October; high pass holds snow late
trails.typical_start_point: Akoyan valley road-head from Soran, or Rawanduz for the official Stage 9 start. Pass sits above hillside orchards; descend to Dargala.
trails.notable: Hindren and Karokh (Korek massif) are 'two great mountains of Kurdistan' in oral tradition. Stage 9 also passes Karak canyon (via ferrata mentioned on the ZMT page) and ends in Saran, rebuilt after Anfal, under sheer rock walls and grape orchards.
trails.uncertainty: A standalone 'Hindren summit trail' with public km was not found. Most visitors cross the saddle rather than bag Hindren's top.
trails.guide_required: Yes
trails.landmine_uxo: Assume caution on old military ground; hire local guide.

trails.nearest_town: Shaqlawa (Şeqlawe), ~50 km northeast of Erbil; also Pirmam
trails.approx_km: Popular day loops 7–17 km depending on ridge length. One public group hike: 17 km, +650 m, 7 hours. Wikiloc Safeen–Shaqlawa: ~12.5 km (7.74 mi) one-way, difficult, ~5h 45m.
trails.season: October–May for cooler ridge walking; summer mornings only. Snow in winter. Spring orchards (pomegranate, fig, walnut).
trails.typical_start_point: Shaqlawa town / resort belt at the foot of the ridge; Mar Gorgees (Mar Giwargis) cave is a known side hike (~500 m of climbing in one local report).
trails.notable: The weekend mountain for Erbil. Long limestone ridge, rock-climbing crags, Saturday group hikes, women's climbing gatherings. Elevation quotes vary wildly (1,166 m on one peak database vs ~1,828 m in local writeups) — it is a long crest, not one cone. Cool-air summer resort town below.
trails.uncertainty: No single official trail. Grade spans easy picnic paths to a full ridge traverse (hard). Elevation of 'the summit' is not consistently published.
trails.guide_required: No for short Shaqlawa paths. Useful for full ridge or cave routes (unmarked).
trails.landmine_uxo: Lower resort slopes are busy. Higher unused ground — don't shortcut blindly.

trails.name_ku: ئامێدی / سەرسەنگ / گەلی شێرانە (Amêdî, Sersing, Gelî Şêrane)
trails.approx_km: Gali Sherana approach commonly described as a ~2-hour hike (drive partway). Amedi citadel / Bere Sili viewpoint / Sulav waterfall are short town walks. Longer Mundi–Khanda Gali type days reported ~6–7 hours.
trails.season: April–October; famous summer-cool destinations. Sarsing is a hill-station.
trails.typical_start_point: Amedi Bahdinian Gate / citadel for town walks; Sulav village for the waterfall resort; Deraluk side for Gali Sherana.
trails.notable: Amedi is a mesa-top historic town (one of the ZMT origin stories was an older idea to start from Amedi's 'gate of Mosul' track). Sulav is a built-up waterfall picnic village. Gali Sherana is the 'hidden paradise' canyon: ice-cold pools, 2-hour hike, heavy local summer use. Sarsing sits on the mountain road as a cool resort.
trails.uncertainty: Not a single marked trail. Sherana '2 hours' is consistently reported but km is rarely published.
trails.guide_required: No for Amedi/Sulav. Useful for Sherana if you don't have a local driver/hike partner.
trails.landmine_uxo: Tourist corridors are used. Side mountains toward the Turkish border are a different (security) story.

trails.name_en: Akre citadel and Newroz hillside walks
trails.approx_km: Town/citadel loops 2–6 km; ZMT Stage 1 adds 16.5 km west to Shush
trails.approx_hours: 1–3 in town; full Stage 1 is a day
trails.season: Year-round. Peak: Newroz (20–21 March) when torchlight processions climb the citadel hill.
trails.typical_start_point: Akre old town / citadel steps.
trails.notable: Not a wilderness trail — the classic urban-mountain walk in KRG. Stone citadel, medieval streets, Newroz capital. Natural pairing with ZMT Stages 1–2 and Villa Kendela (Tariq Kamil Hussein).
trails.uncertainty: None for the town walk.
trails.guide_required: No
trails.landmine_uxo: No for the town.

trails.approx_km: No single official trail. ZMT Stages 6–7 traverse the valley (Harbo–Khalan 20.6 km; Khalan–Soran 26.1 km). Day walks from Barzan village are informal.
trails.approx_hours: Day walks 4–8; ZMT days are longer
trails.season: April–June, September–October
trails.typical_start_point: Barzan village, or ZMT villages Khalan / Qamyran / Harbo.
trails.notable: Heartland of the Barzani tribe. Local conservation ethic (no tree-cutting / hunting) is widely cited. Great Zab river stretches, shared irrigation locks, wildlife. ZMT uses this corridor. Independent blog day-hikes exist but 'freestyle' off-path — not a good idea given UXO.
trails.uncertainty: There is no published 'Barzan National Park trail' with fixed km. Experience is village-to-village.
trails.guide_required: Yes for anything beyond the village.
trails.landmine_uxo: Yes on surrounding heights (see Bradost).

trails.nearest_town: Ahmad Awa village; Khurmal; Halabja. ~84 km east of Sulaymaniyah, Hawraman
trails.approx_km: Picnic/falls: 1–3 km. Pushing the limestone gorge: commonly described as a half-day; treat published '12 km / 1,200 m / 2–3 day' auto-guide figures as unreliable.
trails.approx_hours: 1–2 at the falls; 4–6 if you continue the gorge
trails.season: April–June (best flow and greenery), September–November. Summer is a packed BBQ destination for Slemani families.
trails.typical_start_point: Village/parking at Ahmad Awa on the Zalim (Zallim) River. Shared taxis from Sulaymaniyah (~1.5–2 hours).
trails.notable: Hawraman's classic waterfall: riverside grills, then a real limestone gorge with cold pools and slick rock. One of the few federal-Iraq-adjacent KRG walks that southern Iraqi tourists know by name. Easy access, then optionally more committing.
trails.uncertainty: Grade becomes moderate if you scramble the gorge. Upper-mountain extensions toward the Iranian border are a different trip.
trails.guide_required: No for the falls. Yes for going deep up-canyon or onto the ridges.
trails.landmine_uxo: Falls area is a mass picnic site. Higher Hawraman ridges — local knowledge required.

trails.season: April–June, September–November. Winter is a snow/ice mountain.
trails.typical_start_point: Rest area with huts/taps/toilets at ~1,680 m above Zewe, ~1 hour's drive NW of Sulaymaniyah. Trail starts at a rusty gate ~30 m before the huts.
trails.notable: Slemani's signature peak: official 2,611 m (GPS ~2,602 m), +~1,110 m, Kane Moderate / SAC T4 — steep loose gully, scrambling, huge cliffs and folded strata. Summit sign in Kurdish. Kollaka Bardina cave is a separate ~2.5 hour hike from Hajitan village on the same massif (unmarked). Visible from the highway. Do not hike alone.
trails.uncertainty: Stats from a detailed 2018 trip report (spectacularmountains.com) plus TripAdvisor consensus. Route is cairned in the gully but easy to miss.
trails.guide_required: Strongly recommended (no waymarks, easy to lose the line).
trails.landmine_uxo: Not specifically flagged on the standard Zewe gully; still don't wander onto unused slopes.

trails.approx_km: City-side picnic paths: 3–8 km. Combined Goizha–Azmar ridge walk: 25.3 km
trails.approx_hours: 1–3 for the local hill; 6.5 for the full Goizha+Azmar traverse
trails.season: October–May; summer evenings for sunset picnic. Clear-air days for the city view.
trails.typical_start_point: Western outskirts of Sulaymaniyah, pine-valley path up Goizha.
trails.notable: Slemani's house mountain (~1,512 m accessible high point). Sunset, picnic, 'Slemani' letters on the slope. Ridge has a summit road. True geometric summit occupied by a fenced building — hikers skirt it.
trails.uncertainty: Easy grade is for the standard city ascent. Linking Azmar adds distance and a mine-awareness problem (see Azmar).
trails.guide_required: No for Goizha picnic paths.
trails.landmine_uxo: Lower Goizha is a city hill. Toward Azmar, painted rocks/signs mark mined ground.

trails.approx_km: Usually combined with Goizha as a 25.3 km ridge day; Azmar-only out-and-backs are shorter along the ridge road
trails.season: October–May
trails.typical_start_point: Continue from Goizha ridge road, or drive/taxi onto the Azmar ridge road.
trails.notable: Sister ridge to Goizha (~1,696 m accessible; true summit / Jabal Harutah area is a military telecom site and blocked). Long north–south crest with city and plain views. Part of the same 'Goizha and Azmar Mountains' TripAdvisor listing.
trails.uncertainty: True summit is not a tourist walk.
trails.guide_required: Useful because of mine markings.
trails.landmine_uxo: YES in places. Painted rocks and signs. Do not leave the road/track onto grassy slopes.

trails.approx_km: Shore picnic strolls 1–5 km. Wikiloc 'Dukan hike' near Qalat: ~13.8 km (8.58 mi), ~5–6 hours, moderate, 'nice hike but no access to the lake'. Badawan waterfall: locals say ~2 hours hiking.
trails.season: March–November; famous family picnic destination in spring and autumn
trails.typical_start_point: Dukan town picnic belt / dam viewpoints; Qalat-side hills for the longer loop; Badawan for the waterfall walk.
trails.notable: Iraq's largest lake (Little Zab impoundment). This is overwhelmingly a picnic/swim/kebab landscape, not a waymarked trail system. Named 'Al-Mashtal' / 'Shaykh Ahmed' trails in some auto-guides were not corroborated on official or Wikiloc sources and should be treated as unverified.
trails.uncertainty: HIGH for any specific named trail other than informal lakeside walking and the one public Wikiloc loop.
trails.guide_required: No for picnic shores.
trails.landmine_uxo: Shore resorts are fine. Surrounding unused hills — local advice.

trails.name_en: Qandil range approaches (not a tourist trail)
trails.nearest_town: Ranya / Qaladze side (Sulaymaniyah) and Choman highlands (Erbil) — access is political, not touristic
trails.season: Not applicable as a tourism product
trails.typical_start_point: There is no public trailhead. Checkpoints commonly turn visitors back.
trails.notable: Dramatic 3,000 m+ border range. A local club, Color and Voice of Kurdistan's Nature (CVKN), has hiked in the Qandil mountains (~3 times/month as of a 2021 Kurdistan24 piece), registering trips with the Kurdistan Hiking Federation. That is a local, experienced, permission-based activity — not an open trail.
trails.uncertainty: Do not invent itineraries.
trails.guide_required: Not offered as a standard commercial hike to foreigners.
trails.landmine_uxo: YES, plus PKK presence and recurring Turkish (and sometimes Iranian) military operations. Reddit/local advice: you will likely be turned back at Peshmerga/guerrilla checkpoints.

trails.season: Not a tourism hiking season
trails.typical_start_point: None established for visitors
trails.notable: Culturally and historically important Yazidi mountain. After the 2014 ISIS genocide the area is a reconstruction/security landscape, not a hiking destination. Locals walk the mountain; it is not commonly sold as a tourist hike and should not be listed as one.
trails.uncertainty: Included only to answer the coverage request: it is not a commonly hiked tourist trail.
trails.guide_required: N/A
trails.landmine_uxo: YES — extensive ISIS-era IEDs/mines. Multiple armed actors.

trails.name_en: Federal Iraq Zagros foothills (Khanaqin, Hamrin, etc.)
trails.season: Winter/spring picnic weather only
trails.typical_start_point: None
trails.notable: Not a hiking scene. Federal Iraq's outdoor culture around these foothills is family picnic / river-garden, not trail walking. No well-known public hiking clubs, waymarked paths, or outfitters comparable to KRG were found. Hamrin is low hills; Khanaqin has nearby heights but no documented trail product.
trails.uncertainty: Absence of evidence is the finding. Individual locals certainly walk hills; it is not 'a thing' as organized hiking.
trails.guide_required: N/A
trails.landmine_uxo: Iran–Iraq War legacy in border Diyala is real.

groups.name: Kurdistan Outdoors (Kurdistan Outdoor Tourism)
groups.type: tour operator / outdoor agency (also runs public Friday group hikes)
groups.what_they_run: Pioneer outdoor/experiential agency (public materials say since 2013). Day and multi-day ZMT stages, Friday group hikes from Erbil and Sulaymaniyah (easy–moderate public; hard hikes for experienced people only), cultural tours. Founder Arazu (Arazoo / Arazu Hassan Mohammed) is widely described as Iraq's first female hiking guide. Named ZMT service provider for all stages.
groups.notes: Repeatedly featured in Wanderlust, Travel Tramp, and the official ZMT provider list. Still posting group hikes in 2025–2026.

groups.name: VIKurdistan (Omar / Omer Chomani)
groups.city_base: Choman (operates across the ZMT and Halgurd)
groups.what_they_run: The established Halgurd base-camp and summit operator. Day and multi-day trips on the whole ZMT, homestay/camping logistics, transport back to Erbil. Omar is described on the ZMT site as a pioneer of tourism in Kurdistan/Iraq since the fall of Saddam. Named provider for Stage 13.
groups.notes: Official ZMT provider. Public posts through 2025–2026 including hosting the US Consul General on the ZMT.

groups.name: Gerrok Tourism (Mohammed Alqaderi)
groups.what_they_run: ZMT day and multi-day trips, cultural/private tours across Kurdistan and federal Iraq. Mohammed Alqaderi is one of the ZMT founding partners (NYT 2022 profile of the trail-building). Languages listed: Kurdish, English, Turkmen, Turkish, Arabic.
groups.notes: Official ZMT provider. @wild.mann is the handle listed on zagrosmountaintrail.org; @gerrok.tourism is also in active public use. Confirm which inbox they prefer when booking.

groups.name: Mesopotamia Tourism
groups.what_they_run: ZMT arrangements plus broader Kurdistan/Iraq cultural tours. Languages listed on ZMT: Kurdish, English, Arabic, German, French, Syriac.
groups.notes: Official ZMT service provider. More of a general incoming operator than a hiking club.

groups.name: Untamed Borders
groups.what_they_run: Annual small-group (max ~10) 13–15 day ZMT trek with an international trekking guide plus local crew. Also private/bespoke itineraries. Pre-departure visa/flight advice.
groups.notes: Listed as the international operator on the official ZMT providers page. Public 2026 group-trek marketing exists.

groups.name: Kurdistan Expeditions
groups.what_they_run: Tailor-made Kurdistan and federal Iraq trips: cultural, religious, antiquities, and adventure/hiking (site advertises hiking among its destination categories). TripAdvisor-listed.
groups.notes: Real incoming operator. Instagram handle was not clearly published as a simple @name on the homepage (a numeric IG URL was shown); not invented here. Better known for custom tours than as a hiking club.

groups.name: Iraqi Kurdistan Tour Guide (Ahmad / Ahmed Jalal)
groups.city_base: Erbil (also guides Stage 8 from Garawa as Ahmad Jalal Gawani on the ZMT list)
groups.what_they_run: Private cultural + nature itineraries; Rawanduz/Hamilton Road days; some ZMT walking; Halgurd and multi-day Kurdistan loops for mixed international groups. Very visible on Facebook travel groups.
groups.notes: Likely the same Ahmad Jalal Gawani named on the official ZMT Stage 8 provider list (phone there: +964 750 152 3877). Treat the two numbers as 'confirm on contact' rather than inventing a merge.

groups.name: Iraq and Kurdistan Tours
groups.what_they_run: Guided ZMT sections and general Kurdistan hiking/culture trips. Cited in a 2025 YouTube ZMT vlog as the local fixer.
groups.notes: Public IG + website used by visiting vloggers in 2025. Smaller profile than Kurdistan Outdoors / VIKurdistan.

groups.name: Kurdistan Mountaineering & Climbing Federation (KMCF)
groups.what_they_run: Training, permits (Halgurd summit permits historically routed here), club coordination, festivals (e.g. mass Halgurd climbs). Became a full UIAA member (announced late 2025). Facebook describes it as the body 'for the Kurdistan and Iraq groups and clubs.'
groups.notes: This is the umbrella, not a weekly hike club. Overlaps in press with 'Kurdistan Hiking Federation' / 'Kurdistan Mountaineering Union' — likely the same or successor bodies; naming in English is inconsistent.

groups.name: Color and Voice of Kurdistan's Nature (CVKN)
groups.city_base: Kurdistan Region (Qandil-oriented local club; city HQ not clearly published)
groups.what_they_run: As of a July 2021 Kurdistan24 feature: ~3 hikes a month in the Qandil range, with experienced members, pre-trip training, and registration with the Kurdistan Hiking Federation / local security. Co-founder Hassan Luqman publicly discussed UXO and cross-border fire as the main hazards.

how_to_find.notes: Found via Kurdistan24 (2021). No official Instagram/Facebook handle was confirmed in this research pass — not invented.

groups.notes: Real group in 2021 reporting. 2025–2026 public activity was not independently confirmed. Qandil hiking is not a product to sell to casual visitors.

groups.name: Lutka Mountaineering Group / Destey Lutka Crew
groups.what_they_run: Local peak-bagging and group climbs around Slemani (Piramagrun and nearby hills). Mentioned in 2026 Kurdistan24 coverage of a mass Halgurd ascent and in public mountain-day posts.
groups.notes: Handle appears in public mountain-day posts. Kurdish-speaking club more than an incoming tour desk.

groups.name: Kurdistan Climbing Club
groups.city_base: Erbil (Peshmerga Park wall; also Slemani outdoor wall at Hawary Shar Park)
groups.what_they_run: Sport climbing, not long-distance hiking. Friday sessions; indoor/outdoor walls. Included because it is one of the few named, currently public outdoor-sport clubs.
groups.notes: Climbing, not trekking. Useful sibling to the hiking scene.

groups.name: Zagros Mountain Trail village guides and homestays (collective)
groups.city_base: Along the ZMT (Shush, Akre, Hashtga, Safti, Alka, Harbo, Khalan, Qamyran, Soran, Rawanduz, Saran, Dargala, Rezan, Choman)
groups.what_they_run: Stage-by-stage guiding, dinners, rooms. This is the actual on-trail labor of the ZMT. Standout named people on the official provider page: Nader Zaher Mustafa (Shush mayor/homestay); Sadiq Khuder Izzo (Stages 1–2 guide); Tariq Kamil Hussein / Villa Kendela (Akre); Anwer Salih Muhammad (Safti); Jawad Ibrahim Meer (Qamyran, Barzan valley, founding stakeholder); Ahmed Ibrahim Muhammad (Rezan, described as the benchmark guide); Ahmed Mustafa Hassan 'Hama Soor' (Dargala); Omar Chomani (Choman/Halgurd).
groups.notes: Phones are published on the official page. Contact through that list or via the Erbil operators who book them. Do not treat random WhatsApp forwards as official.

groups.name: Halgurd Mountain Guide (public Facebook page)
groups.what_they_run: Weekend Halgurd summit trips, mixed international groups (public 2025 posts: Bulgarian group, Norwegian guests, open DMs).

how_to_find.facebook: Halgurd Mountain Guide (facebook.com/groups and page posts under this name)

groups.notes: May overlap with Omar Chomani / other Choman guides. Identity of the page admin was not uniquely verified. Real and posting; treat as a lead, not a legal entity name.

not_found_or_weak.query: University hiking clubs (Salahaddin, University of Sulaimani, Duhok)
not_found_or_weak.finding: Student outing culture exists and '100+ hiking groups / 7,000+ members' was claimed by Kurdistan Chronicle, but no stably named, currently public university club with a verified handle was confirmed. Many groups organize only via closed Facebook/WhatsApp.

not_found_or_weak.query: Federal Iraq hiking outfitters (Baghdad, Khanaqin, Basra mountains)
not_found_or_weak.finding: No equivalent of the KRG scene. Southern/central visitors come TO Kurdistan to hike and picnic.
Other than ZMT GPX downloads, almost nothing is blazed. Korek resort paths and city hills (Goizha, Safeen picnic tracks) are the exception.
